clue.text: Appreciative watcher gives tongue

definitions.meaning: a spectator who shows approval by applauding with the hands
the metal striker that swings inside a bell is called its tongue

explanation.surface: A pleased spectator finds their voice and speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives' is a link word; 'tongue' here is not speech but the swinging part inside a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: someone who applauds, and the striker hanging inside a bell.

clue.text: Charles writing for openings

parts.note: Chas is the usual short form of the name Charles
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Charles takes up a pen to apply for job vacancies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deep gaps or fissures in the ground are openings.

clue.text: Sharp detectives in rising American intelligence organisation

indicators.note: the detectives are placed inside the turned-round agency name
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the USA
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Clever detectives have infiltrated a growing American spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' only makes sense in a down entry, where the agency reads upwards; the detectives sit inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an acidic taste or remark is sharp, tart or biting.

clue.text: Can-opener?

parts.note: can is slang for jail, so the thing that opens a jail is its entrance barrier

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool for opening tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: the barrier through which inmates enter or leave the can, meaning jail.

clue.text: General carries sovereign's weapon

indicators.note: the widespread word holds the coin's symbol within it

parts.note: general, meaning widespread, is a synonym of rife
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A general officer bears the monarch's firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is an adjective (widespread), not an army officer; a sovereign is an old British gold pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-barrelled gun is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Miss tea when involved in painting

indicators.note: involved means twisted up or tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist so absorbed in work that the tea break goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a canvas by the French artist Henri, known by his surname, is a painting.

clue.text: Growing row over a speaker

parts.note: a line of hair grown on the upper lip, above the mouth, which is the speaker

explanation.surface: An argument escalates about someone giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line, not a quarrel, and 'speaker' is the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: facial hair grown in a line above the lip, which sits over the mouth.

clue.text: System for better transport

definitions.meaning: a better is a person who bets; a totalisator is a betting system pooling stakes
to carry or lug something about

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the totalisator betting pool, and a verb meaning to carry.

clue.text: Being sly they last out

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cunning people are the ones who survive longest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting secretively and furtively is being sly.

clue.text: The way the world goes round

definitions.text: The way the world goes round

parts.words: The way the world goes round
parts.note: the earth spins from west towards the rising sun, so this is its direction of rotation

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark about how life works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is a direction, not a manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: the planet rotates towards the east, so that is the way it turns.

clue.text: Excuse for party in capital

indicators.note: the party sits inside the word for excellent

parts.note: capital as an adjective means excellent, first-rate, which is A1, written AI
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A politician's excuse for being at a party in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is the old British exclamation meaning first-rate (A1), not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a claim of being elsewhere at the time is an excuse.

clue.text: If results go astray, efforts may well be

definitions.text: If results go astray, efforts may well be

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: When the outcome goes wrong, the work was in vain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: efforts with no good results are in vain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unproductive or futile efforts bear no fruit.

clue.text: Make use of one's time at home

indicators.note: to make use of these words is to rework them into a new order

parts.note: one's is read as ONES, so the fodder is all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone spends their spare hours at home productively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make use of' is an unusual anagram signal; the apostrophe in 'one's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat on two floors with its own entrance is a kind of home.

clue.text: What you have here, say, is for hanging a hammock

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: what the solver is reading is a crossword clue

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue about rigging a hammock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes the solver's 'clue' into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: the cords at each end by which a sailor's hammock is suspended.

clue.text: Teacher after a job for a demanding employer

indicators.note: the teacher is put after the job in the answer

parts.note: a task is a job
a schoolmaster, or master, is a teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher pursuing a post with a strict boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a boss who imposes heavy workloads is a demanding employer.

clue.text: Charge rates, otherwise someone will attend uninvited

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Charge an entry fee, or freeloaders will turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a party crasher is a person who turns up without being asked.

clue.text: Takes a meal among sailors, though it causes delay

indicators.note: the eating word goes inside the sailors

parts.note: tars is a slang term for sailors
to dine is to take a meal

explanation.surface: Sailors are late back because they stop to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lateness or slowness is what holds things up.

clue.text: He settles without recourse to law

definitions.text: He settles without recourse to law

parts.words: He settles without recourse to law
parts.note: settles means takes up residence; one who occupies property without legal right

explanation.surface: A man resolves a dispute out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' suggests resolving a dispute; here it means moving in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: someone who occupies an empty building without legal permission.

clue.text: He's unlikely to be found missing

definitions.text: He's unlikely to be found missing

parts.words: He's unlikely to be found missing
parts.note: missing means failing to hit a target, so this is an accurate shot

explanation.surface: A dependable man who never goes absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' means failing to hit, not being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: a skilled shot rarely misses the target.

clue.text: Suit for naval officers

definitions.meaning: a card suit is thirteen cards, a fourth of the pack
the part of a ship's upper surface reserved for officers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is cards, not clothing for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one fourth of a pack of cards, and the officers' area at a ship's stern.

clue.text: Fire when an explosive's not set to start?

indicators.note: not says a piece is left out of the explosive
the omitted piece is at the beginning of the explosive

parts.note: gelignite is a blasting explosive
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Firing an explosive charge before it is primed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ... to start' removes GEL from the front of GELIGNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set alight or kindle is to fire.

clue.text: Arrival of a head of department at opening

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A new departmental head turns up at a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the coming of something is its arrival.

clue.text: Bird rears others

indicators.note: rears suggests something turned back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A bird raising its young or the young of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Either bird could be the answer; the crossing letters decide which is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The diving seabirds of the north are other birds, so here they are the others.

clue.text: Daughter is accused, but let off

parts.note: charged means formally accused of a crime

explanation.surface: A daughter faces charges but walks free.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses fit: a released prisoner is let off, and a fired gun is let off.

clue.text: Status of a holy man in church

indicators.note: the holy man piece is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: The standing of a cleric within the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hereditary social class determines a person's standing.

clue.text: Pen note making a personal complaint

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A writer pens a letter of grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is an enclosure, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an inflamed swelling on the eyelid is an ailment of one's own.

clue.text: Femme fatale — one working for a time on her hair

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A seductive woman's hairdresser is only a temporary worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a seductive, dangerous woman is a siren or seductress.

clue.text: Junk food?

definitions.meaning: cow's stomach lining eaten as a dish

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: nonsense or rubbish, and the edible stomach lining of cattle.

clue.text: They scout about one side of Glasgow

definitions.meaning: patrollers of forests or parks who range about, or senior members of the Guides
a Glasgow football club, one half of the Old Firm rivalry with Celtic

explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow's two big football teams are Celtic and Rangers, so one 'side' is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: patrolling wardens who roam an area, and a Scottish football team.

clue.text: Listener heads home in determined mood

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone who hears the call makes for home, resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' is a link (goes towards); 'in' is part of the idiom 'in earnest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in a serious, resolute state of mind is being in this.
